8.type_documentation: Expand description An inert request to collect a complete traversal, returned by request.collect_all(maximum_pages) . Awaiting it yields every item only after the controller proved exhaustion ( PageStep::Done ) within the effective bound. Reaching the bound while a valid continuation exists returns a Pagination / CompletionLimitExceeded error carrying the summary ( PageBound / NextRequestKnown ); a success never contains an undisclosed prefix. Any other failure fails the whole collection. Controls (timeout, caps, cancellation) may be applied before awaiting. Dropping the started future cancels the traversal through its drop guard.

8.type_documentation: Expand description A caller-driven lazy traversal returned by request.pages(maximum_pages) . Construction is inert. The first polled next_page future of a nonzero traversal allocates the aggregate operation identity and starts one absolute deadline covering controller start, every page and attempt, and all time the application spends between polls; it is never reset per page. There is no background prefetch and at most one page fetch is active. Pages does not implement RequestControls and has no timeout or cancellation setters: apply controls to the originating request before calling .pages() . The captured cancellation tokens can still be cancelled externally after the traversal started. § Cancellation Dropping a next_page future that was never polled changes nothing. Dropping a next_page future after it was polled cancels the whole traversal through a synchronous drop guard: its in-flight work is dropped and the summary records StopReason::Cancelled . Later next_page calls return Ok(None) ; budgets are never replenished. An attached cancellation signal observed before or during a fetch returns one Pagination / Cancelled error, then Ok(None) . A fetch error is returned exactly once; later calls return Ok(None) and the summary retains StopReason::Failed . Dropping a started traversal records cancellation, never EOF or rollback. This strict rule is deliberate: a resumable cancellation mode would need durable pending-page accounting and is not provided.

methods.method.next_page: Source pub fn next_page ( &mut self, ) -> impl Future <Output = Result < Option < Page <Item>>, ApiError >> Fetches, validates and delivers the next page, or returns Ok(None) once the traversal is exhausted, bounded, finished, failed or cancelled. See the type-level documentation for cancellation rules.
methods.method.finish: Source pub fn finish (self) -> TraversalSummary Ends the traversal and returns its final summary. An already terminal Exhausted , PageBound , Failed or Cancelled state is preserved; otherwise the traversal records StopReason::Application . An unstarted traversal keeps no operation identity and emits no observation.

9.type_documentation: Expand description A managed, owned, bounded accepted response body consumed lazily. § Acquisition is not end of body An endpoint await that returns a ByteStream has only validated the accepted head and opened the stream: the operation’s completion reports StreamOpened and ApiResponse::body_disposition reports BodyDisposition::StreamOpened , never a completed download. Later failures belong to the stream, not to the already fixed operation result, so an operation is never reported as fully successful and then failed for the same body. § Ownership and lifecycle The handle exclusively owns the native body; it is not Clone . Consume it with next (or the [ Stream ] implementation), inspect it with summary and stop early with finish , which never drains the body. The terminal StreamState is Eof only after the caller observed the actual end of the body. A terminal failure yields exactly one error, then None ; the failure is retained in the summary. Dropping the handle before a terminal result records cancellation and synchronously drops the native body. § Cancellation of next Dropping an individual pending next future does not terminate the stream. Poll state, acquired-byte accounting and the idle baseline live in the handle; a later next resumes the same acquisition and never resends the request. This deliberately differs from pagination, where dropping a started page fetch terminates the traversal. External cancellation signals attached to the originating request ( cancel_with ) cancel the entire stream: the next poll yields one Cancelled error and releases the body. § Finite lease After acquisition the stream holds a finite lease (5 minutes total and 30 seconds cumulative idle by default, configurable through RuntimeConfigBuilder::stream_lifetime / stream_idle_timeout and narrowed by CallOptions::cap_stream_lifetime / cap_stream_idle ). The total lease includes consumer pauses between polls; idle counts only time while an underlying read is pending, nonempty data resets it and empty chunks do not. A pending read keeps its idle baseline when its next future is dropped, and once its idle budget is spent that read can no longer complete: data or an end of body that becomes available only afterwards yields one IdleTimeout error, not the data and not a clean end. Likewise a read observed to complete only at or after the end of the total lease yields one LeaseExpired error instead of its data or a clean end; when both limits have run out, LeaseExpired takes precedence. Empty chunks acquire no data, so the acquisition stays pending across the cooperative yield described below: the time until the next poll counts as idle, also when next is dropped at that yield. A whole-operation timeout cap ( CallOptions::cap_timeout ) started at the first request poll also bounds the lease; without it, the request timeout ends at acquisition. Expiry is observed on the next poll (or while a read is pending, through one handle-owned timer); a stream that is never polled again releases its native body on drop. No detached task is started and there is no implicit forever mode or reconnection. § Limits and framing Every yielded chunk is nonempty and passed the cumulative decoded (post-decompression) byte limit; the first excess chunk is withheld. Empty transport chunks are suppressed, at most MAX_EMPTY_RESPONSE_CHUNKS consecutive empties are accepted, and at most 32 are handled per poll before yielding to the scheduler. No policy retry, authentication recovery or native replay happens after handoff: a reconnecting application must start a new operation. § Errors and sensitivity Every stream error carries FailureStage::StreamConsumption , DispatchKnowledge::ResponseObserved , the original endpoint, operation, attempt and status, and a StreamSummary . Errors, Debug and the summary never contain body bytes, headers or URLs. § Runtime The stream must be polled inside a Tokio runtime with time enabled, as is every Concord operation.

methods.method.next: Source pub fn next (&mut self) -> impl Future <Output = Option < Result < Bytes , ApiError >>> Returns the next nonempty chunk, None after the end of the body or after the one terminal error. The returned future is cancel-safe: dropping it leaves all acquisition state, counters and the idle baseline in this handle, and a later call resumes the same acquisition.
methods.method.finish: Source pub fn finish (self) -> StreamSummary Stops consumption without draining and returns the final summary. After the actual end of the body the Eof state is preserved, as is an earlier Failed or Cancelled state; otherwise the stream records Application and drops the native body unread.

9.type_documentation: Expand description A managed, owned lazy stream of semantic records decoded incrementally. ItemStream<T> owns a managed ByteStream and one request-local record decoder whose framing strategy is hidden. It shares every byte-level contract of ByteStream : acquisition is not end of body, the finite total lease and pending-read idle limit, consecutive empty-chunk guardrails, the decoded byte limit, external cancellation, and no retry or replay after handoff. It is not Clone . § Records and framing Each record’s staged bytes are bounded by the smaller of the decoder’s max_buffered_bytes and the runtime frame limit (1 MiB + 2 bytes by default, RuntimeConfigBuilder::stream_frame_limit ); the first excess byte is rejected before it is retained and the oversized record is never yielded. At most the runtime record limit (100,000 by default, stream_max_records ) is yielded; the next record is withheld with a correlated error. Transport chunks are never record boundaries. The decoder owns final-record policy at end of body (for example NDJSON parses a final nonempty line without a newline exactly once; CSV rejects an unterminated quote), and an incomplete tail is an error, never a silently dropped record. A partial stream never becomes a complete success. § Lifecycle and cancellation next is cancel-safe exactly like ByteStream::next : the decoder buffer, poll state, counters and idle baseline live in this handle, so dropping a pending next future does not terminate the stream and a later call resumes it, unless the idle budget of that pending read ran out in the meantime: record data or an end of body (which could otherwise complete a staged final record) that becomes available only after the idle limit yields one IdleTimeout error. Record data or an end of body observed only at or after the end of the total lease likewise yields one LeaseExpired error and never completes a staged record. A body read failure, framing or decoding failure, record/frame/byte limit, lease or idle expiry, or external cancellation yields exactly one correlated ApiError , then None . The summary counts full yielded records; finish never drains and preserves Eof after the final record. Dropping the stream before a terminal result records cancellation and synchronously drops the decoder, staged bytes and native body. § Sensitivity Records are application data owned by the caller. Errors, Debug and the summary never contain records, staged bytes, decoder state or parser text.

methods.method.next: Source pub fn next (&mut self) -> impl Future <Output = Option < Result <T, ApiError >>> Returns the next complete record, None after the final record or after the one terminal error. The returned future is cancel-safe: dropping it keeps the decoder buffer, counters and idle baseline in this handle.
methods.method.finish: Source pub fn finish (self) -> StreamSummary Stops consumption without draining and returns the final summary. After the final record was observed the Eof state is preserved, as is an earlier Failed or Cancelled state; otherwise the stream records Application .

10.type_documentation: Expand description A successful semantic value together with its logical response metadata. This is the single metadata wrapper for buffered values, bytes, no-content, byte streams, record streams, and application-defined outputs. Its Debug implementation is structural: it never formats T , the logical URL, or any response header value. Accessors intentionally expose the actual accepted headers and credential-sanitized logical URL to application code, which owns later logging and storage. Public URL values may still contain operational identifiers or personally identifiable information.

10.type_documentation: Expand description Safe request metadata supplied to a selected rate limiter. The request carries the complete effective conjunctive plan with protected canonical keys, the value-free schema of every policy ( crate::rate_limit::RateLimitPolicy::schema ), and the limiter capability that core snapshotted at client build. Together, each policy schema and Self::capability form the complete schema descriptor of RATE-05: policy ID, ordered labels and encoding IDs, framing version, canonical window schema, and limiter namespace/algorithm identity. It never carries request bodies, credentials or raw headers.
